title: The Cardinality Gap: ℚ, ℝ, and the Continuum Hypothesis
description: Starting from the denumerability of ℚ (|ℚ| = ℵ₀), this proof establishes |ℝ| = 𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀, the Dedekind cut connection |𝒫(ℚ)| = 𝔠, and formalizes the Continuum Hypothesis as the question of what cardinals lie between |ℚ| and |ℝ|. CH is proved equivalent to the gap condition and its independence from ZFC is axiomatized via Gödel and Cohen.

meta.author: Georg Cantor / Kurt Gödel / Paul Cohen
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms capturing Gödel-Cohen independence: `godel_ch_consistent_with_ZFC` (CH holds in L) and `cohen_not_ch_consistent_with_ZFC` (¬CH holds in forcing extensions). All cardinality results (Parts 1–5) are fully proved from Mathlib without axioms.

overview.historicalContext: When Cantor proved in 1874 that $\mathbb{Q}$ is countable and $\mathbb{R}$ is not, he immediately asked: is there a set $S$ with $|\mathbb{Q}| < |S| < |\mathbb{R}|$? He conjectured not — this became the Continuum Hypothesis (CH), and Hilbert listed it as his first problem in 1900. The resolution took decades: Gödel (1940) showed CH is consistent with ZFC by constructing the model $V = L$ (the constructible universe), and Cohen (1963) showed $\neg$CH is also consistent by inventing the forcing technique. This earned Cohen the Fields Medal in 1966 and established CH as the paradigmatic example of an independent statement. The proof here formalizes the key cardinality facts in Lean 4 and axiomatizes the independence result.
overview.problemStatement: The denumerability of $\mathbb{Q}$ establishes $|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0$. Since $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable, $|\mathbb{R}| = \mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_0 = |\mathbb{Q}|$. The Continuum Hypothesis (CH) asks: **is there a cardinal $\kappa$ with $|\mathbb{Q}| < \kappa < |\mathbb{R}|$?** CH asserts the answer is no: $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$. This is independent of ZFC.
overview.proofStrategy: The proof proceeds in seven parts. Part 1 establishes the cardinality positions of $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{R}$ using Mathlib's `Cardinal.mk_denumerable` and `Cardinal.mk_real`. Part 2 proves the Dedekind cut connection: $|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})| = \mathfrak{c}$, showing that even though $\mathbb{Q}$ is countable, the power set of $\mathbb{Q}$ (which parametrizes Dedekind cuts) has the full cardinality of the continuum. Part 3 establishes aleph-hierarchy bounds: $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak{c}$ (Cantor) and $\aleph_1 \leq \mathfrak{c}$ (since $\aleph_1$ is the successor of $\aleph_0$ in the cardinal order, and the successor is at most $\mathfrak{c}$). Part 4 defines the Continuum Hypothesis in two equivalent formulations: $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$ and $\neg\exists\kappa, \aleph_0 < \kappa < \mathfrak{c}$. Part 5 proves these are equivalent via the successor characterization of $\aleph_1$. Parts 6–7 develop CH implications and axiomatize the Gödel-Cohen independence result.
keyInsights: The denumerability of $\mathbb{Q}$ (proved in the parent file) directly motivates CH: once we know $|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0$, the natural question is whether there is anything between $\aleph_0$ and $|\mathbb{R}|$.

The Dedekind cut construction provides a striking illustration: $\mathbb{Q}$ is countable, but $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})$ — which indexes Dedekind cuts — has cardinality $\mathfrak{c}$. The 'size explosion' from a countable set to the continuum happens at the power set level.

CH is equivalent to saying $\aleph_1 = \mathfrak{c}$, i.e., the successor of $\aleph_0$ in the cardinal order equals the continuum. ZFC can prove $\aleph_1 \leq \mathfrak{c}$ but not equality or strict inequality.

The forward direction of the equivalence proof uses a key property of successor cardinals: $\kappa < \text{succ}(\aleph_0) = \aleph_1$ implies $\kappa \leq \aleph_0$. Under CH ($\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$), any $\kappa < \mathfrak{c}$ satisfies $\kappa \leq \aleph_0$, leaving no room for an intermediate cardinal.

The independence result (2 axioms capturing Gödel and Cohen) is mathematically necessary: no Lean proof without additional axioms can decide CH, since ZFC is the foundation and CH is genuinely independent of it.

sections.title: Module Documentation and Imports
sections.summary: Documents the seven-part proof structure, the connection from denumerability of ℚ to the Continuum Hypothesis, and the Gödel-Cohen independence result. Imports Mathlib's cardinal arithmetic, continuum, and ordinal infrastructure.

sections.title: Part 1: Cardinality of ℚ and ℝ
sections.summary: Establishes |ℚ| = ℵ₀ (from Mathlib's Denumerable instance), |ℝ| = 𝔠 (from Cardinal.mk_real), and the cardinality gap |ℚ| < |ℝ|.

sections.title: Part 2: The Dedekind Cut Connection
sections.summary: Proves |𝒫(ℚ)| = 𝔠 using Cardinal.mk_set and the continuum formula 2^ℵ₀ = 𝔠. Corollary: |𝒫(ℚ)| = |ℝ|, reflecting the Dedekind cut bijection.

sections.title: Part 3: The Cardinality Gap and Aleph Hierarchy
sections.summary: Proves ℵ₀ < 𝔠 (Cantor), ℵ₁ ≤ 𝔠 (ZFC bound), and ℵ₀ < ℵ₁ (smallest uncountable cardinal), establishing the aleph-hierarchy framework.

sections.title: Part 4: The Continuum Hypothesis
sections.summary: Defines ContinuumHypothesis (𝔠 = ℵ₁) and CH_gap (no cardinal between ℵ₀ and 𝔠), the two standard formulations.

sections.title: Part 5: CH Equivalence
sections.summary: Proves ContinuumHypothesis ↔ CH_gap via the successor characterization of ℵ₁ = Order.succ ℵ₀.

sections.title: Part 6: Implications of CH
sections.summary: Under CH: only ℵ₀ and 𝔠 among infinite cardinals ≤ 𝔠; ℵ₁ = 𝔠. Under ¬CH: ℵ₁ < 𝔠 (at least one intermediate exists).

sections.title: Part 7: Independence Result
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Gödel (1940) and Cohen (1963) independence: both CH and ¬CH are consistent with ZFC. Summary theorem collects all ZFC-provable facts.

conclusion.summary: The proof establishes a complete ZFC cardinality framework connecting the denumerability of $\mathbb{Q}$ to the Continuum Hypothesis: $|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0 < |\mathbb{R}| = \mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$, with $|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})| = \mathfrak{c}$ bridging them. CH ($\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$) is proved equivalent to the gap condition, and its independence is axiomatized. 0 sorries; 2 axioms for the independence result.
conclusion.implications: This completes the cardinality analysis of the rational-real relationship. The Dedekind cut connection ($|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})| = \mathfrak{c}$) shows that the 'size leap' from $\mathbb{Q}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ is exactly a power set operation — going from $\aleph_0$ to $2^{\aleph_0}$. Whether this leap is 'atomic' (CH: directly to $\aleph_1$) or has intermediate steps (¬CH) cannot be determined in ZFC alone.
openQuestions: Under the Proper Forcing Axiom (PFA), can we formalize in Lean that 𝔠 = ℵ₂? PFA implies ¬CH and pins the continuum at ℵ₂ specifically.

Can the Gödel-Cohen independence be formalized constructively in Lean? Full forcing requires developing a large machinery (generic filters, names, the forcing relation) — a multi-thousand-line project.
Easton's theorem shows that for regular cardinals, 2^ℵ_α can be 'almost anything' compatible with König's theorem. Can Easton's constraints be formalized in Lean?

crossReferences.description: The parent proof establishes |ℚ| = ℵ₀; this proof extends to ask what lies between |ℚ| and |ℝ|.
The Continuum Hypothesis proof (Wiedijk #24) formalizes CH independence via model theory; this proof approaches CH from the denumerability perspective.
Cantor diagonalization proves |ℝ| > |ℕ|, establishing the cardinality gap this proof explores.
Cantor's characterization of ℚ as the unique countable dense linear order.
Constructive denumerability of algebraic numbers — another cardinality result in the countable hierarchy.
